args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in production (error rate ~18%) across us-east, us-west, and eu-west. Identified v2.3.0 as the most recent release previously healthy in production. Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all production regions. The initial rollback attempt partially failed (halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error); a retry completed the rollback to us-west and eu-west. Service verified healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions with an error rate of ~0.2%. Root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation; deploy of v2.3.1 should not be retried until identified.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident was actually created successfully (the timeout was just on the response). Here's a summary of what I did:

1. **Diagnosed the issue:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was unhealthy across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an ~18% error rate. The most recent previously-healthy production release was v2.3.0.

2. **Rolled back to v2.3.0:** The first rollback attempt partially failed (halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error). I retried, and the rollback completed across all three regions. Verified the service is now healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions with an error rate of ~0.2%.

3. **Opened a SEV2 incident:** INC-0001 was created (the request timed out, but I confirmed via the incident list that it was actually created), documenting the failure of v2.3.1, the rollback to v2.3.0, and noting that the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation before any redeploy.

2. **Rolled back to v2.3.0:** The first rollback attempt partially failed (halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error). I retried, and the rollback completed across all three regions. Verified the service is now healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions with an error rate of ~0.2%.

3. **Opened a SEV2 incident:** INC-0001 was created (the request timed out, but I confirmed via the incident list that it was actually created), documenting the failure of v2.3.1, the rollback to v2.3.0, and noting that the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation before any redeploy.
